caption: The drawing depicts a group of people in a scene that appears to be set indoors, on a reddish-brown and tan background. On the left side, a figure dressed in red and blue garments sits elevated on a platform or stage, with one arm outstretched; this figure wears a hat and is positioned behind a red curtain. In front of this platform, a series of steps descend to where several other figures stand. These figures are dressed in a mix of red, blue, brown, and tan, with some wearing hats and others bareheaded. Near the center, two figures are holding another figure by the arms, guiding or restraining him; this central figure wears a light tan garment and has shoulder-length dark hair. Another figure next to them appears to be holding a large, white, jug-shaped object. There are additional figures to the right, also dressed in similar earth tones and blue, with some holding spears or staffs. The composition is densely packed with figures positioned in close proximity, and the color palette consists mainly of earthy browns, reds, blues, and tans. The background includes drapery and architectural elements, and the overall style is painterly with visible brushstrokes and soft edges. There is text at the top left reading "JESUS IS CONDEMNED TO DEATH".
title: Station of the Cross No. 1: "Jesus is Condemned to Death"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
